occurrences.source_excerpt:
Overview of endocrine system
• “Glands” in human body can be divided into endocrine glands and exocrine glands.
• Endocrine glands: ductless glands that secrete hormones into blood
• Exocrine glands: glands that secrete nonhormone chemicals to a surface through ducts
• Sweat gland, skin sebaceous gland, and gastric gland are examples of exocrine glands.
• Only endocrine glands belong to “endocrine system”.

Mechanisms of Hormone Action
• Hormones are carried by blood to all tissues. However, not all cells are affected by 1 hormone.
• The cells, that are affected, are “target cells” of a certain hormone.
• These cells have specific receptor proteins in cytoplasm or in cell membrane.
• Hormone molecules bind to receptor proteins and trigger a series of changes of these cells.

source_pages.document_title: Lecture 7 - Endocrine System and Hormone Regulation (July 2026)

occurrences.source_excerpt:
Mechanisms of Hormone Action
• Mechanisms of water soluble hormones:
• (1) Bind to “plasma membrane receptors” on cell membrane
• (2) Trigger increase of different “second messengers” inside the cell
• Examples of common second messengers include cAMP, calcium ions, cGMP, etc.
• (3) Second messengers activate or inactivate enzymes inside cytoplasm.
• (4) Cellular activities are changed!

occurrences.source_excerpt: Overview of endocrine system • “Glands” in human body can be divided into endocrine glands and exocrine glands. • Endocrine glands: ductless glands that secrete hormones into blood • Exocrine glands: glands that secrete nonhormone chemicals to a surface through ducts • Sweat gland, skin sebaceous gland, and gastric gland are examples of exocrine glands. • Only endocrine glands belong to “endocrine system”.

Overview of endocrine system
• “Glands” in human body can be divided into endocrine glands and exocrine glands.
• Endocrine glands: ductless glands that secrete hormones into blood
• Exocrine glands: glands that secrete nonhormone chemicals to a surface through ducts
• Sweat gland, skin sebaceous gland, and gastric gland are examples of exocrine glands.
• Only endocrine glands belong to “endocrine system”.

Mechanisms of Hormone Action
• Mechanisms of lipid soluble hormones:
• (1) Bind to “intracellular receptors” in cytoplasm or in nucleus
• (2) Hormone-receptor complex binds to a specific DNA region
• (3) A specific mRNA is produced from certain region of DNA.
• (4) The mRNA leaves nucleus and attaches to ribosomes on rough ER.
• (5) New proteins are produced to change cellular activities.

Mechanisms of Hormone Action
• Hormones are carried by blood to all tissues. However, not all cells are affected by 1 hormone.
• The cells, that are affected, are “target cells” of a certain hormone.
• These cells have specific receptor proteins in cytoplasm or in cell membrane.
• Hormone molecules bind to receptor proteins and trigger a series of changes of these cells.
